newsitem.title: USA: Staples to buy Kingfisher stakes in joint ventures.
newsitem.headline: Staples to buy Kingfisher stakes in joint ventures.

text.p: Staples, Inc., the office superstore chain, said Wednesday it has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Kingfisher PLC's stakes in the companies' two European joint ventures for $50 million.

Staples will take full control of Staples UK, a 50-50 partnership that operates 34 stores in Britain. It will also increase its ownership of Maxi-Papier, which operates 16 stores in Germany, from about 50 percent to about 90 percent.
Staples will assume an additional $6 million in bank debt after the purchases from Kingfisher, a British retailing group, the company said.
The transactions are expected to close in May 1997.
"The full integration of both businesses into Staples, Inc. will give us more potential to enhance their operating performance," said Thomas G. Stemberg, chairman and CEO of Staples.
"Second, we will now be able to work toward even greater scale economies with respect to purchasing on both a European and global basis, as well as optimizing our management and tax structures."

Staples, based in Westerborough, Mass., operates 555 office products superstores in over 100 markets across the United States and Canada under the names Staples, Staples Express, Business Depot and Bureau En Gros.
Staples' stock edged down 18.75 cents to $18.875 early on Nasdaq.
